# Question answer: generator-shortcuts, version 1

> For this generator, name the strongest plausible shortcut or rival rule that fits the canonical demonstrations. Give an exact input on which it disagrees with the intended rule, how you checked the output, and whether your proposed generator emits such cases.

**Rival.** Copy the top-left 3×3 template only at blue marker centers on the fixed canonical lattice: `(r - 1) % 3 == 0` and `(c - 5) % 3 == 0`, using zero-based coordinates. Leave other markers alone. This is plausible because every marker in the four labeled canonical pairs lies on that lattice. Fresh Racket checks establish that this rival matches **4/4 canonical outputs**.

**Exact emitted counterexample.** Final generator version `3.1.1`, seed `11`, sample index `2`, difficulty `medium`, with no overrides, emits the following fully specified input.

Input: **9 rows × 17 columns.** Output: **9 rows × 17 columns.** Begin with zeros, fill all of column `3` with gray `5`, put this template in rows `0..2`, columns `0..2`, and put blue `1` at `(2,9)`, `(2,12)`, `(2,15)`, `(5,12)`, and `(5,15)`. All other cells remain zero.

```json
[[8,6,6],[6,6,8],[8,9,6]]
```

None of the five markers lies on the canonical lattice. The rival therefore leaves this input unchanged. The intended Racket rule copies the template at all five centers, producing **45 differing cells**; for example, zero-based cell `(1,8)` is `8` under Racket and `0` under the rival. The full input, exact Racket output, exact rival output, and all differing coordinates are retained in `checks/shortcut/witness.json`.

**Verification and emission.** `checks/shortcut/probe_final_shortcut.py` executed the four canonical inputs and this generated witness through public `Catalog.apply(reference="canonical", check_generator_domain=True)`: **5/5 valid Racket outputs**, all generator-domain checks valid. The receipt is `checks/shortcut/racket.json`, and `checks/shortcut/commands.json` records the command and exit `0`. The witness is an ordinary default `anti_lattice` slot at schedule index `2`; no input mutation or override was needed. The default five-slot schedule is canonical, canonical, anti-lattice, anti-lattice, anti-lattice.

These checks bind to generator SHA-256 `75ee24dc86a6d294fab9aab46fc47392cab0b7f5dbdaa58a59e63b349acf83c9` and canonical rule hash `63b41fa0b187`. They demonstrate this concrete shortcut and its emitted refutation, without claiming uniqueness against every possible rival.
